### Observed differences

- Work on activities A01, A03, A13, A14, A17 and A22 was carried out by a substantially different set of resources in the later window. In the earlier window, User_46 held the largest single share of executions on these activities (roughly 7–10 in 100, peaking at about 10.5 in 100 on A22), while User_41 held no leading share anywhere; in the later window, User_39 rose to about 8–13 in 100 on every one of these activities and User_41 took about 5–7 in 100, while User_46 fell to at most about 4.5 in 100 and several resources that previously led dropped out of the leading shares entirely. The broad remainder pool stayed large in both windows (roughly 38–52 in 100). Each of these resource profiles differs from about 1999 of 2000 random re-splits of unchanged data. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]
- A10 moved from concentrated to dispersed handling. In the earlier window, a small set of resources carried out about 86 in 100 A10 executions (largest single share about 17 in 100), with only about 14 in 100 going to the remaining pool; in the later window, each former lead resource fell to about 10 in 100 or less and the remaining pool absorbed about 52 in 100. [ASSIGN003]
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A09 and A04 changed in shape rather than in typical length. In the earlier window, 132 such gaps averaged about 0.017 hours (roughly 1 minute) with very little spread (standard deviation about 0.005 hours); in the later window, 105 gaps were observed, the median lengthened only slightly (about 1.0 to 1.2 minutes), but the spread grew about twenty-fold (standard deviation about 0.116 hours, i.e. roughly 7 minutes), so the mean roughly doubled to about 0.032 hours — a heavy tail of long gaps drives the average. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a change in resource allocation: the execution of A01, A03, A10, A13, A14, A17 and A22 shifted from one set of resources to another. In the earlier window these activities were handled chiefly by resources that in the later window hold only minor shares (User_46 the most visible example), while resources that previously held little or no leading share — most visibly User_39, together with User_41 — took over the largest shares; A10 additionally dispersed from a small dedicated group into a broad pool. Supporting signs: the resource family produced 7 qualifying items against 0.007 expected by chance if nothing had changed (roughly a thousandfold excess), every item's difference exceeds about 1999 of 2000 random re-splits, and the same resources gain and lose across all seven activities, which per-activity sampling noise would not produce; the shares rest on 133–270 occurrences per activity and window. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show why the allocation shifted. An important competing explanation is that the mix of cases reaching these activities changed and different kinds of cases are handled by different resources; no control-flow indicator qualified (0 items against 0.17 expected), so this cannot be checked here. A13 and A14 show numerically identical profiles and may reflect a single underlying shift rather than two; much of the gain sits in the unlisted remainder pool, so the full destination of the work is only partly visible; and the resource codes are anonymous, so no roles or teams can be inferred. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]

Other differences: a timing change in its own right — gaps between consecutive completions of A09 and A04 kept a similar typical length (median about 1.0 to 1.2 minutes) but became far more uneven, with long gaps frequent enough to double the mean (about 0.017 to 0.032 hours) and about 20% fewer consecutive pairs observed (132 vs 105). This rests on a single indicator (1 time item against 0.015 expected by chance), and whether it is connected to the allocation change cannot be determined from this evidence. [TWAIT001]
